pr_body:
on shutdown, the jdk's InnocuousThread can try to change a thread name. This requires `"java.lang.RuntimePermission" "modifyThread"` permission. However InnocuousThread doe not inherit any Access Control Context and therefore have no permissions. This results in AccessControlException.
This commit fixes this by skipping a check for modify thread permission if a thread is innocuous.
relates #91658 and #91650

When previously described AccessControlException is thrown, it is not being catched anywhere in the Elasticsearch, hence it ends up being handled by `ElasticsearchUncaughtExceptionHandler#onNonFatalUncaught`
This is being again being run by the `thread [process reaper]` which is an innocuous thread (jdk specific) and has no permissions. `onNonFatalUncaught` is trying to log a message, but this in turn requires `java.lang.RuntimePermission" "getenv.*"` permission. which is does not have. This again results in `AccessControlException java.lang.RuntimePermission" "getenv.*"`

We can fix this by executing with doPrivileged  in  ElasticsearchUncaughtExceptionHandler#onNonFatalUncaught and this will stop the Security Manager's walk and will have ES's global grant permissions.

closes #91650

So it turns out that the thread calling for `"java.lang.RuntimePermission" "modifyThread"` is a `thread [process reaper (pid 84882)]` That exception stacktrace in logs is not showing what the full stacktrace was. When adding additional debug logs I see

We can fix this by skipping to check for permission if the thread is **Innocuous**  and we do a similar check already in this method.
```
        if(isInnocuousThread == false){
            checkPermission(MODIFY_THREAD_PERMISSION);
        }
```


With those two changes I don't get these exceptions anymore

I think this will take care of the issue I opened: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/91658 for the innocuous thread. I can dup mine here if we are going to handle both of these fixes under this issue.

> I still don't know why the Thread.dispatchUncaughtException does not have the permission for getenv.*

All the frames on the stack are from code sources that hold the permission, but still the access check fails, why?  Every java thread has an optional inherited AccessControlContext - which is the ACC captured by its creator. This inherited ACC limits the set of permissions that the thread runs with - it's implicitly checked for each full-stack walk. The j.lThread javadoc has more details on it. 

In this particular case the thread, the reaper thread, is a JDK platform thread - it is also an innocuous thread (JDK-specific) and as such has an inherited ACC that hold no permissions - it's empty. It is this inherited ACC that causes the permission check to fail. 

> I think that we should add doPriviliged in ElasticsearchUncaughtExceptionHandler#onNonFatalUncaught

Agreed.  This will stop the permission check from going further - to the inherited ACC of the innocuous thread.

I'm not exactly sure why this all started happening now, but the situation seems well-understood and aforementioned changes seem reasonable.

@tlrx This is helpful, and it promoted me to look again at WHY this started happening recently. In JDK 19, the reaper thread was changed to be an innocuous thread, see https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8279488, therefore its inherited ACC has no permissions ( where it previously inherited from whatever thread triggered its creation ).

FTR - I started a conversation on the core-libs-devs OpenJDK mailing list relating to the JDK 19 change of process reaper threads to be innocuous, which resulted in the adverse affect when terminating the Elasticsearch server - https://mail.openjdk.org/pipermail/core-libs-dev/2022-November/097029.html.
